chapter: Gambling, Cab's small groups and Havana
title: Havana nightlife and visiting stars
summary: Francis says Havana never slept; they recall late-night food and visits from Nat Cole and Woody Herman's group.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Those were some beautiful days. What did you think of Cuba? I thought it was a beautiful country in those days.
Well, I'll tell you. you know,
during those days, people used to talk about Paris, but I really don't think that Paris stood a chance with Havana, because the town just never slept.
Oh, there is no night like a Cuban night.
That's right. We used to get off and go to the bar and we'd be drinking there and the guy would give us food -- the cold cuts.
Oh yes, (inaudible) and those hot olives and peppers. Wasn't that great? And all the musicians would get off at four or five o'clock in the morning, and eat.
Yep, and stay until the sun come up.
Until the sun came up; that's right.
Some beautiful days, man. I tell you. I really enjoyed my association with him and seeing so many artists down there; remember Nat Cole came down one time?
Yeah, Nat Cole, Woody Herman -- remember Woody Herman and his small group?
Yeah. With Shelly Manne, Ernie Royal, Milt Jackson.
Yeah, Milt Jackson and Red Mitchell.
Right. That's right; on the bass.
It was nice seeing Red Mitchell in Nice, France this summer.
Oh, wow, what a beautiful guy.
He was a beautiful human being, man.
Yes, sir, and he hasn't changed at all, either; he's still the same smooth, beautiful man.
Oh yes, I have so many nice memories and it was just so nice going through with you for a second.
